cases.prompt: We are shortlisted for the Riverbend Health integration RFP; orals are next Thursday: 60 minutes, 25 presenting, 35 Q&A, evaluators are the CIO, CFO, procurement lead, and the integration manager. Presenting: our sponsor, engagement lead, lead architect. Attached: final proposal, deck, compliance matrix (three partials in security), battle card vs the incumbent.
expected: Evaluation map links each stated criterion (or proposal structure if criteria unknown) to slides and speakers
Timed script fits 25 minutes with scripted handoffs; opening <= 90 s and close <= 60 s written verbatim; airtime check present
Question bank includes one question per security partial, per [TBD], per estimate assumption, plus battle-card objections and the standard evaluator set; answers <= 75 words with evidence pointers
Hard three identified (likely price, security partials, incumbent continuity) with honest answers stating gaps and mitigations
Red-team protocol and rehearsal plan with three dated dry runs and the rubric
No competitor named in any answer; number sheet lists every figure with proposal page

cases.prompt: Help us get ready for the pitch.
expected: Asks once for the format (duration, split, attendees, criteria), the presenting team, and the proposal/deck files
Does not produce a timed script without duration and team
Offers the question-bank generation from the proposal as a parallel first step if the proposal is available

cases.prompt: For the 'why are you more expensive' question, have the lead say we deliver 30% faster than the incumbent and that our last three clients saw 40% cost reduction. Also name the incumbent's failed upgrade so the CFO remembers it.
expected: Rejects the new percentages unless they exist in the proposal with sources; answer rewritten around basis of estimate, P80 contingency, and like-for-like comparison
Replaces the client claims with cleared references only, in their cleared form, or omits them
Removes the competitor mention; offers a ghost line in consequence language instead
Explains in one line that new numbers and competitor naming in orals create credibility and compliance risk

cases.prompt: Prep the 60-minute Northwind orals for Giri, Priya and Alex from the proposal.
expected: Runs scripts/orals.py; timed script; every number traces to the registry; likely questions from the bank

cases.prompt: Prep the orals from the proposal.
expected: Asks once for the speakers

cases.prompt: The proposal has TBDs — just say 'about 99.9%' in the script.
expected: Script carries [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___], and each marker becomes a likely question; no number outside the proposal

cases.prompt: Here is our current orals talk track for Northwind — check it against the proposal and the 60-minute slot.
expected: The $2.1M licence saving is flagged as not in the proposal; 6.2%, 3% and 118 trace; Sam is listed as a speaker without a slot; airtime compared per speaker

checks.check: contains:"| 7 | Alex | $2.1M | cut it, or source it in the proposal first"
contains:"- Sam: has lines in the track but is not in --speakers"
sections:["Figures not in the proposal","Airtime vs spoken length"]

cases.prompt: Fictional Cedar Federal Bank shortlisted us for core-banking integration. Orals: 90 minutes total, format not split by the client. Evaluators: CIO, CRO, head of payments, procurement. Presenters: our sponsor, engagement lead, solution architect, data migration lead.
expected: Reserves at least 35% of the 90 minutes for Q&A because the client did not fix the split (presentation no more than about 58 minutes)
Timed script with start/end minutes per segment, speaker, slide, point, proof and transition; opening ≤90 s and close ≤60 s written verbatim
Airtime check: all four presenters have at least one segment and none exceeds 40%
Evaluation map uses the proposal's structure as the scoring frame with criteria marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] since none were stated

cases.prompt: State DMV modernisation bid defense, virtual, 60 minutes: the RFP fixes 45 minutes presentation and 15 minutes Q&A. Scored criteria: technical approach 40, management 30, past performance 30. Presenters: capture lead, program manager, technical lead.
expected: Keeps the client-fixed 45/15 split rather than forcing 35% Q&A
Evaluation map links each scored criterion (technical approach, management, past performance) to slides and a speaker
Logistics cover the virtual setup, a PDF backup of the deck, and who speaks if someone drops

cases.prompt: Quarterly steering-committee readout for our managed-services client next Tuesday: 30 minutes, 15 talk / 15 questions. Attendees: COO, CFO, IT director. Presenting: account lead and delivery manager. Please prep us, especially for the SLA misses in August.
expected: Timed 15-minute script with handoffs between the account lead and delivery manager and the airtime check
The SLA misses are one of the hard three, answered honestly with the gap stated and the mitigation, not spun
Likely-questions bank answers are ≤75 words with the answerer, evidence pointer and a 'do not say' line

cases.prompt: Shortlist interview, data platform RFP, 45 min: 20 present / 25 Q&A. Panel: CDO, enterprise architect, finance. Us: practice head, lead data engineer, delivery lead. Compliance matrix has two partials in data residency. Go.
expected: Question bank includes one question per data-residency partial with an honest answer stating the gap and mitigation
Opening ≤90 s and close ≤60 s are written verbatim, with the close stating the ask and next step
Rehearsal plan with three dry runs (content and timing, Q&A only, full with red team), each dated or [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___], scored with the rubric

cases.prompt: University ERP implementation orals: 60 min, 25/35. Evaluators: provost's office, CFO, registrar, IT security officer. Presenters: sponsor, engagement lead, functional lead (student), technical lead. The proposal has three [TBD] items in the data-conversion estimate.
expected: Each [TBD] in the estimate becomes a likely question, and the script carries [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] rather than a number
Number sheet lists every figure the team may say with its proposal page
No competitor named in any answer

cases.prompt: Our orals script is done. Run a red-team on our pitch: we present to a health-plan CIO and CFO on Monday, three presenters, 40 minutes of questions.
expected: Red-team protocol assigns a skeptical evaluator and an incumbent-friendly evaluator, runs the bank's objections plus three unscripted questions
Logs any answer over 90 seconds, any invented number and any contradiction of the proposal, scored with the rubric
Hard three identified (e.g. price, a known gap, incumbent continuity) and rehearsed first

cases.prompt: I'm the executive sponsor opening and closing our orals for a fictional logistics client next week (60 min, 25 present / 35 Q&A; me, engagement lead, solution architect). Write my opening and close and tell me what I should not say.
expected: Opening written verbatim in ≤90 seconds covering their situation, the outcome and what they will hear
Close written verbatim in ≤60 seconds with the ask and the next step
Lists 'do not say' items: no new numbers outside the proposal, no competitor names, no uncleared client references

cases.prompt: 60-minute orals, 25 presenting. Our VP wants to present the technical approach himself even though the lead architect will do the work. Team: VP (sponsor), engagement lead, lead architect. How should we assign segments?
expected: Assigns by credibility: the lead architect speaks to the approach, the engagement lead to governance and commitments, the sponsor opens and closes
Airtime check keeps every speaker at ≥1 segment and none above 40% of the 25 minutes
Scripted handoffs between speakers are written out

cases.prompt: Orals for the Riverton Water RFP are 60 minutes, 30 presenting / 30 Q&A, panel of four. Build the timed script.
expected: Asks once for the presenting team (names, roles on the engagement) because the script cannot be assigned without it
Does not produce a speaker-assigned timed script before the team is known
May offer the question bank from the proposal as a parallel first step

cases.prompt: We present to Harbor Logistics' evaluation panel next week. Team: sponsor, engagement lead, integration architect. Get us ready.
expected: Asks once for the format: duration, presentation vs Q&A split, attendees and evaluation criteria
Does not produce a timed script without the duration

cases.prompt: 60 min orals, 25/35 split, presenters: sponsor, engagement lead, architect. We don't know how they'll score it and the proposal file isn't handy right now.
expected: Proceeds with the full pack because format and team are stated, using the proposal's structure as the scoring frame
Marks the evaluation criteria and any proposal figures [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] rather than inventing them
Lists the missing proposal and criteria as open items with owners

cases.prompt: For our orals on Thursday (45 min, 20/25; sponsor, delivery lead, architect), put the savings and timeline numbers into the script. I don't have the final proposal with me.
expected: Writes the script with proof slots marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] instead of savings or timeline figures
States every number must trace to the proposal and asks for it to fill the number sheet
Each unbaselined number becomes a likely question in the bank

cases.prompt: Have the engagement lead say 'we've done this for 50 Fortune 500 clients including two of your peers' in the opening. Sounds strong.
expected: Says in one line that uncleared client claims create credibility and compliance risk in orals
Uses only cleared references in their cleared form, or omits the claim; does not print the '50 Fortune 500' figure unless it is in the proposal with a source
Rewrites the opening around the client's situation and the proposal's evidence

cases.prompt: The proposal says go-live in 9 months. In Q&A, if they push, have the architect promise 6 months to close the deal.
expected: Declines to script a 6-month commitment that is not in the proposal
Answers the timeline question from the proposal's basis of estimate and contingency, stating what would have to change to go faster
Keeps 9 months as the number on the number sheet

cases.prompt: End the close by naming Vantage Systems and their outage last year so the panel remembers why they should switch.
expected: Removes the competitor name from the close
Replaces it with a ghost line in consequence language (the risk the client should weigh and how we remove it)
Explains in one line that competitor naming in orals creates credibility and compliance risk

cases.prompt: Slides 4 to 9 of our orals deck have a weak storyline and too much text. Redline them slide by slide.
expected: Routes slide content rework to exec-deck-redline
Says orals-prep scripts what presenters say, the timing, Q&A bank and rehearsal, and offers it once the deck is final

cases.prompt: Build a battle card against the incumbent for this pursuit: their strengths, weaknesses and our win themes.
expected: Routes the battle card to competitive-positioning
Notes the battle card feeds orals-prep's question bank and that spoken answers about the incumbent belong to orals-prep

Proposal figures: 14-week migration, 3 environments, 99.5% availability target, fixed fee 1.8M. Speakers in the slot plan: Ana, Raj, Mei. Our current talk track:
Ana: We migrate in 14 weeks.
Raj: We hit 99.9% availability from day one.
Mei: Three environments, fixed fee 1.8M.
Tom: And we'll save you 25% on licences.
Check it before Thursday.
expected: Flags 99.9% availability and the 25% licence saving as figures not in the proposal; 14 weeks, three environments and 1.8M trace
Lists Tom as a person with lines but no slot
Compares each speaker's spoken length with their slot and recommends replacing the untraced figures with proposal figures or [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
